subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw support implicit state-dir `.backupignore` loading and partial external-asset exclude semantics in `backup create`, or require an explicit opt-in/smaller first version before merge?
rationale: This changes backup safety and restore semantics for existing state directories, and the code currently exposes a warning-only gap for external assets; automation cannot choose that product/security contract for maintainers.

options.title: Require explicit scoped excludes
options.body: Keep `--exclude` and `--exclude-file`, but remove implicit `.backupignore` loading and make the first landed version either apply excludes to every asset root or clearly limit the CLI contract.

options.title: Accept warning-only external gaps
options.body: Merge the feature with `.backupignore` auto-load and external-asset warnings as an intentional first version, owning the restore/security tradeoff in release notes and follow-up tracking.

options.title: Pause for backup redesign
options.body: Hold this PR and solve backup scope, progress, streaming, and exclude semantics together in a smaller maintainer-sponsored design.

recommendation.title: Require explicit scoped excludes
recommendation.body: Keep `--exclude` and `--exclude-file`, but remove implicit `.backupignore` loading and make the first landed version either apply excludes to every asset root or clearly limit the CLI contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup command and infra history makes this the best available routing candidate for the CLI/backup behavior decision, though ownership is shared.
